# A route parameter and a root component's state var, reaching one route.
#
# The two arrived from different directions and meet in `newRouteGC`. #215
# hoists a root component's `var` onto the window the component lifts, so the
# route's expression context is scoped to that window or `hits` renders as a
# bare name the emitted Go never declares. But the window is also what carries
# the binding its path parameters arrive in -- and that one is bound from the
# URL the request arrived on, per request, not per session.
#
# So the window scope has to answer for one and not the other: `hits` is a
# field of the per-session State, `v` is the handler local
# `writeRouteParamBindings` declares. Scoped without that split, the parameter
# came out as a field of a State struct that had no business carrying it --
# and it compiled, because `routeStateVars` had put the field there too.

sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out app.sngl

exec go build ./...

# The parameter is the local, the state var is the field.
grep 'v.Id = __r.PathValue\("id"\)' out/server.go
grep 'html.EscapeString\(v.Id\)' out/server.go
grep 's.Hits' out/server.go

# And the parameter is not a field of it.
! grep 's\.Id' out/server.go

-- go.mod --
module rootparam

go 1.24

-- srv/srv.go --
package srv

func Bump(n int) int { return n + 1 }

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import nav "sngl:ui/nav"
import "go:rootparam/srv"
import "sngl:platform/html"

struct PageParams {
    id string
}

component main root {
    var hits = 0

    ui.window(title=pages.current.title) {
        nav.stack #pages {
            nav.page #page(href=`/p/{id}`, title="t", params=PageParams{}) {
                component content(v) {
                    html.button(innerText="go", @click { hits = srv.Bump(hits) })
                    html.span(innerText="{v.id}")
                    html.span(innerText="{hits}")
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

main()
